sources.entry: SwingMusic - Swing Music is a beautiful, self-hosted music player and streaming server for your local audio files. Like a cooler Spotify ... but bring your own music. (Source Code) MIT Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: Swing Music is a self-hosted music streaming server and browser-based player for your own local audio files, with an Android client.
summary.what_it_does: Swing Music scans a music folder you provide and serves it through a browser-based UI, with an Android mobile client available for streaming from a phone. It normalizes metadata to keep the library consistent and groups albums into versions (such as Deluxe or Remaster). It offers daily mixes based on listening activity, related artists and albums, and a folder view for browsing by directory. Other features include collections for grouping albums and artists, listening statistics, Last.fm scrobbling, silence detection combined with cross-fade, and multi-user support. The README lists Windows, Linux, and arm64/x86 as supported platforms, with macOS marked as coming soon.
use_cases: Streaming a personal local music library to a browser or phone
Self-hosting a Spotify-like player for your own files
Sharing a music server with several household users
Scrobbling local listening history to Last.fm
Browsing a music collection by folder structure
Running a music server on a home NAS or Docker host
how_to_run: On Linux or macOS: curl -fsSL <install script URL from README> | bash (URL is missing from the README text)
On Windows: download the portable build from the downloads page and run it
Docker Compose: image ghcr.io/swingmx/swingmusic:latest, map port 1970, mount /path/to/music to /music and /path/to/config to /config
Docker CLI: docker pull ghcr.io/swingmx/swingmusic:latest, then docker run with -p 1970:1970 and the same volume mounts
Open the app URL in a browser to configure and use Swing Music
Set SWINGMUSIC_PORT and SWINGMUSIC_DEVICE_NAME environment variables to change port and reported device name
notable: Album versioning that links normalized albums with labels such as Deluxe or Remaster
Silence detection combined with cross-fade for seamless playback
Daily mixes generated from listening activity
Folder view for browsing the library by directory
caveats: macOS support is listed as coming soon in the README
The Android client is a separate download, and the README does not describe its setup
Contributing is open, but the README points to external guidelines and a Telegram group
keywords: play local mp3 files in browser
